title: Decidability of the infinite target discounted-sum problem
formal: Is there an algorithm which, on any rational inputs \(0<\lambda<1\) and a,b,t, terminates and decides whether there exists an infinite sequence \(w\in\{a,b\}^{\mathbb N}\) satisfying \(\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}w_i\lambda^i=t\)?
definitions:
Rationals are encoded by signed binary integer numerators and positive binary integer denominators. The inputs a, b and t may be positive, negative or zero, and a=b is allowed. The infinite sequence is unconstrained: it need not be periodic, computable or generated by a finite automaton. Since its entries come from a finite bounded set and 0<lambda<1, the series converges absolutely. The first entry has coefficient one. Equality to t is exact.

The requested algorithm is a total deterministic Turing machine on valid finite input encodings, with no prescribed time bound. This is an existence decision, not a request to output the sequence or approximate its sum. Replacing infinite words by finite words, eventually periodic words or a random generator changes the problem.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked decision algorithm and a termination and correctness proof, or prove undecidability. Numerical approximation of the attainable set does not decide exact membership at every rational target.
context:
The corrected expanded treatment distinguishes finite target sums from infinite sequences and links the latter to rational expansions and affine dynamics.

The stochastic counterpart computes probabilities of exact sums; a zero-probability witness may still exist, so that result does not answer this existential question.
why: This elementary-looking arithmetic existence question is a barrier in discounted quantitative verification.

import_provenance.original_title: Decidability of the infinite target discounted-sum problem
import_provenance.original_statement: Given rational numbers 0<λ<1 and a,b,t, decide whether an infinite sequence wᵢ∈{a,b} satisfies Σᵢ≥0wᵢλⁱ=t. This is the arithmetic obstruction studied in Raskin’s work on rational verification of discounted-sum games.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: The finite-word version and special discount factors are decidable. The September 2026 probabilistic Markov-chain result concerns a different variant and does not settle this existence question: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.03670 .

sentences: Each term of an infinite discounted series is chosen from two rational values.
The question asks whether the sum can equal a supplied rational target exactly.
Witnesses may be nonperiodic and need not have finite descriptions.
The desired algorithm must terminate on every valid rational input.
Finite-word and stochastic variants have results that do not settle this target.
